capture.source: Existing local.26 overlay status log, from latest startup; no new game captures
limitations: Signal timestamps are app receipt/logging times, not physical user input or game animation completion times.
This measures the pre-reader stage; excludes screenshot recognition and simulation.
findings: Native fs.watch already wakes the log reader; 1000 ms polling is fallback, not the normal trigger path.
First readiness probe starts at max(250,450*pace) ms and only if the remaining deadline is at least 900 ms.
At Speed-up pace=0.45, a 1500 ms rule waits 675 ms and does not start the early readiness probe.
Ready-worker currently converts the full frame, blurs it, scores the board and reads cells/controls for each of three observations; the previous saved-frame benchmark measured 301 ms per probe.
Every matched trigger advances the readiness epoch, including later UI events for the same action.

priority: Port the upstream rule changes and measured tables into both JS and Rust; regenerate WASM and invalidate incompatible MC caches.
Separate action-start signals from presentation/ready events so repeated UI events do not erase readiness evidence for the same action.
Use a bounded cheap region-based readiness stage, followed by one full semantic board validation; retain unchanged-screen rejection and cancellation.
Enable the cheap stage for short Speed-up waits and measure the first-trigger-to-capture distribution on live transitions before claiming gains.
